title: Once upon a time
goal: Tell what has happened, as you see or hear it, with -(Y)pdYr, and follow the start of a tale.

intro.text: For an action you didn't see, known from its result or from others, add `-(Y)p` and `-dYr`: *Ol gelipdir* (He's come, I see), *Ýagyş ýagypdyr* (It has rained). For **they**, *-lAr*: *gelipdirler*. Tales tell their story this way.

vocab.en: to tell (a story); to talk about

exercises.question: You come home and see your brother's bag by the door. Which sentence says you know he's here from what you see?

why.1: *geldi* is the plain past, as if you saw him come or simply state it.

exercises.explain: *gel-* + *-ip* + *-dir*: *gelipdir*, he has come, as you can see.

exercises.label: *gitmek* with `-(Y)pdYr`: he has gone, they have gone (I hear)
exercises.explain: *git-* softens its *t* before the vowel of *-ip*: *gidipdir*. For **they**, add *-ler*.

exercises.en: It has rained. (The ground is wet.)

reject.why: *ýagdy* states it plainly, as something you saw. For what you can tell from the wet ground: *ýagypdyr*.

exercises.explain: *ýag-* + *-yp* + *-dyr*: *ýagypdyr*, it has rained, as you see.

accept: Apparently Merjen has lost her key.
Merjen has lost her key, I hear.
It seems Merjen has lost her key.

exercises.explain: *-üp* rounds in the second syllable after *ö*; *-dir*, the third, doesn't: *görüpdir*.

exercises.prompt: The guests have already arrived, I see.

reject.why: *geldiler* states it plainly. For what you see from the result: *gelipdirler*.
The ending follows the front vowel of *-dir*: *gelipdirler*.

exercises.prompt: Atam bize bir erteki gürrüň berdi.
exercises.text: My grandfather told us a tale.

exercises.prompt: Bir gün patyşa bir düýş görüpdir.
accept: One day the king had a dream.
One day the king had a dream, they say.

exercises.question: Where did the boy go one day?

context.tk: Bir bar eken, bir ýok eken, bir obada bir garyp oglan bar eken.
context.en: Once upon a time, in a village, there was a poor boy.
One day he went to the market.
At the market he saw a bear.

why.1: There is no king in this part: *ol bazara gidipdir*.
why.2: He lives in a village, and goes *bazara*, to the market.

exercises.explain: *Bir gün ol bazara gidipdir*: one day he went to the market.

exercises.prompt: She has gone to Mary, I hear.

reject.why: *git-* softens its *t* before the vowel of *-ip*: *gidipdir*.
*gitdi* is the plain past. To pass on what you heard: *gidipdir*.

accept: The child has gone to sleep.
The child is asleep, I see.
The child has fallen asleep, I see.

exercises.prompt: My grandfather told us a story.
accept: Atam bize bir hekaýa gürrüň berdi.

reject.answer: Atam bize bir hekaýa gürrüň beripdir.
reject.why: You heard it yourself, so the plain past: *gürrüň berdi*.
